column1: # tests/shares.tsv — THE SHARED RESOURCES a gate may name in its `# SHARES:` line (#370, 14z-225; maintainer-ruled
# 2026-11-08: "A1: today, written down (Recommended)", "B1: every gate has the line (Recommended)", "C1: yes, host-wide
# lock (Recommended)"). A registry of RESOURCES, not of gates: which gates hold a token is read from the gates.
# Every registered gate carries exactly one header line (docs/project/gate_header_contract.md § `# SHARES:`):
#   # SHARES: <token> [<token> …]          this gate's jobs hold these; `self` = its own jobs never overlap each other
# Both runners never run two jobs holding one token at once (tests/lib/share_pool.py); a gate holding a token of this
# registry also claims it on the HOST (tests/lib/shares.sh vs_shares_claim: an OS file lock per token held by
# tests/lib/share_lock.py for the claiming shell's lifetime, re-entrant for a
# run nested under its holder), so a hand run or a second tier on the same host is kept apart too.
# Held by tests/test_shares.sh: every token here is held by at least one gate, every token a gate names is here or
# `self`, and a gate holding one of these makes its claim call (the third column).
# token<TAB>wait seconds (how long a claim waits for a live holder before REFUSED, exit 3)<TAB>the call a holding gate makes (the census looks
# for it on a code line, with the token when the call is vs_shares_claim)<TAB>what it protects and how a gate holds it
